title: Ohio Secretary of State Blackwell Allocates Voting Machines to Favor Bush in Swing State
summary: J. Kenneth Blackwell, Ohio's Secretary of State and co-chair of President Bush's re-election campaign in the critical swing state, oversaw a deeply flawed election marked by systematic misallocation of voting machines that created unprecedented long lines disproportionately affecting Democratic and minority voters. In Franklin County, predominantly Democratic precincts (where Gore won 70%+ in 2000) had 17 fewer machines in 2004 and 20% more voters per machine than Republican precincts, while the strongest GOP precincts received 8 additional machines. The Washington Post reported that '27 of the 30 wards with the most machines per registered voter showed majorities for Bush.' Nearly three-fourths of Democratic precincts had higher-than-average voters per machine, compared with only 30% of GOP precincts. County election directors testified that Blackwell's office failed to provide adequate funds for poll worker training and deluged local officials with last-minute administrative orders that caused confusion, especially in Ohio's biggest cities—traditional Democratic strongholds. Blackwell also instructed officials to reject voter registration forms not printed on 80-pound cardstock and maintained his position as chief election official despite obvious conflicts of interest. Voters sued in King Lincoln Bronzeville Neighborhood Association v. Blackwell, alleging Blackwell 'allocated election resources in a racially discriminatory manner' leading to vote dilution, ballot cancellation, and disenfranchisement through long lines and mechanical difficulties.
